Write a rattler-build recipe for a package

Source: R/conda.R
conda_recipe.Rd

Generates a rattler-build recipe.yaml from the package's DESCRIPTION, for publishing to a conda channel such as prefix.dev. The recipe is a build artefact rather than a file to commit: it builds from the package directory as it stands, so building an older release means checking out its tag and generating again.

Imports and Depends become host and run requirements, LinkingTo host only. Base packages are dropped, the R version comes from the r_base variant at build time. List Bioconductor dependencies in a Config/devforge/bioconductor field (comma separated) so they map to bioconda's bioconductor- names. Your own packages need no mapping, add their channel when building.

A package with src/rust/Cargo.toml gets the Rust compiler and has CARGO_BUILD_TARGET unset before the install: conda's Rust activation sets it, which moves the static library under target/<triple>/ where rextendr's Makevars does not look. Windows is skipped.

Usage

conda_recipe(pkg = ".", dir = file.path(tempdir(), "conda"), .verbose = TRUE)

Arguments

pkg

String. Path to the package root. Defaults to ".".

dir

String. Directory to write recipe.yaml into. Created if needed. Keep it outside pkg, the build copies pkg as its source. Defaults to a temporary directory.

.verbose

Boolean. Report what was written. Defaults to TRUE.

Value

The path of the recipe, invisibly.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
recipe <- conda_recipe(".")
system2("rattler-build", c("build", "--recipe", recipe, "-c", "conda-forge"))
} # }
